_comment: How the app host routes a request. Read once at server start.
mode: 'dispatcher'  A single catch-all answers every path that has no route folder of its
own. This is what the current app needs: /reports/<key>,
/management/<entity> and /p/<slug> are dynamic, so they cannot be URL
folders. The dispatcher below handles them.
mode: 'crawler'     ONLY per-URL route folders answer. /hello is served by
ahscripts/routes/hello/route.ts and by nothing else; a path with no
folder of its own is a 404. Use this to host a different frontend: the
host serves whatever folders it finds and holds no opinion about the app.
dispatcher           the catch-all script, used only in dispatcher mode. The host's own
per-URL folder resolution is tried FIRST in both modes, so a route
folder always wins over the dispatcher.
A missing or unreadable file means 'dispatcher' with the default path, which is exactly how the
app behaved before this file existed. An unrecognised mode also falls back to dispatcher, and
says so in the log, because the catch-all is the more permissive of the two.
This is MECHANISM: it names no route, no page and no business rule.
